name: DDGameAss
summary: Goal-driven Doomsday assistant with versioned game knowledge, safe semantic planning, evidence provenance, OCR, vision, and macro automation.
description: Windows desktop Doomsday assistant that separates game-domain understanding, confidence-aware perception, versioned rules, safe semantic planning, supervised outcomes, and legacy macro execution.
notes: Moved into the shared Codex workspace from F:/Zombi/macro_controller.
Doomsday modules expose reusable OCR, dataset bootstrap, and vision primitives for sibling projects.
An emerging Doomsday crawler service for roster discovery and provider-aware hero enrichment is now explicitly exposed for Knowledge support and integration.

The 0.5 intelligence core introduces 15 modes, 18 versioned rulesets, goal constraints, semantic actions, evidence conflicts, provider isolation, an execution policy gate, outcome evaluation, and a dedicated learning store.
Knowledge remains the owner of source ranking; DDassistant publishes a validated Doomsday SourceRegistry overlay and consumes ranking through an adapter.
Concrete macro execution remains disabled by default until the conflicted macro database and structural UI-node recognition gaps are resolved.
The field roster planner records current and proposed Doomsday march pairings, including heroes, beasts, special-weapon notes, bench candidates, and development priorities.
Runtime inventory tracks the legacy Android-x86 VirtualBox VM, installed BlueStacks instances, and the active Windows client without starting emulators or ADB.
The supervised roster acquisition port captures the visible game UI, normalizes OCR into provenance-aware atomic contributions, and defers canonical roster writes to user confirmation.

The field roster planner now records a concrete five-march transition: Maxwell plus Daryl, Felix plus awakened Chasey, retained Rubina investment, and Metok Tso as a measured future comparison rather than an automatic pairing.
The GUI exposes a read-only GamePlan preview and the planner no longer treats unexecuted action effects as observed state.
Hero-interface learning now records crash-safe click journals and quality-checked full frames while keeping semantic labels and automation evidence-gated.
The live roster pipeline uses immutable artifacts, explicit preview and decisions, confirmation, optimistic atomic commit, history, audit, and an evidence outbox.
Tesseract CLI provides local ita+eng OCR; only the home Eroe label is calibrated until full hero-view frames are reviewed.

Semantic campaigns attribute reusable macro sequences to an explicit objective, operation, asset domains, game version, validation state, and immutable sequence snapshot without granting execution authority.
Campaign runs persist pre/post observations and evidence independently from playback, so success informs coverage without granting authority to a macro.
Network observation uses project-local mitmproxy in local PID mode with TLS passthrough, redacted metadata-only JSONL, no trusted CA, no Windows proxy mutation, no replay and no protection bypass.

The native client must be launched through C:/Users/Public/Desktop/Doomsday.lnk, which resolves to DoomsdayLastSurvivors.exe; direct Doomsday.exe execution is explicitly unsupported because it returns error 0x4.
